advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `--check-only` actually run `check_scanners` (or remove the no-op branch) so its OK verdict cannot be produced when scanners are absent.
evidence: scripts/install_review_scanners.py:394: `if args.check_only:`
scripts/install_review_scanners.py:395: `print(f"review scanners check-only: OK ({entry.platform})")`
scripts/install_review_scanners.py:396: `return 0`
Contrast with the real `check` mode at line 406 which calls `check_scanners(entry, prefix)` and runs `_run_version` on both binaries. The `--check-only` path never asserts any producer ran.
advisory.finding: The `--check-only` mode in `main()` (without `--gitleaks-archive`) prints a success message and returns 0 WITHOUT calling `check_scanners` — it never verifies the installed gitleaks/semgrep binaries exist or match the pinned versions. Its 'OK' verdict is produced identically whether the scanners are correctly installed or entirely absent, so this branch fails open.
scenarios: A caller invokes `install_review_scanners.py --check-only` expecting a real installed-scanner health check and receives OK on a machine with no scanners installed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a positive `_safe_extract_gitleaks` test: build a tar whose gitleaks member is named with a nested/`..` path, extract, and assert the binary lands exactly at `<destination>/gitleaks` and is mode 0o755.
evidence: scripts/install_review_scanners.py:244-249: `member = next((m for m in tar.getmembers() if Path(m.name).name == GITLEAKS_BIN), None)` … `member.name = GITLEAKS_BIN` … `tar.extract(member, destination)`

tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py:739-750 (`test_gitleaks_extract_rejects_archive_without_binary`) is the ONLY test touching `_safe_extract_gitleaks`, and it asserts the error branch only — the extract/chmod path and the member.name normalization never run.
search of tests/ for `member.name` / `traversal` returns no test that a traversal-named gitleaks member is neutralized to `destination/gitleaks`.
advisory.finding: scripts/install_review_scanners.py _safe_extract_gitleaks has only a negative test (archive without a gitleaks binary); its security-relevant happy path — the `member.name = GITLEAKS_BIN` reassignment that neutralizes any leading path/traversal in the archived member, followed by extract + chmod 0o755 — is never exercised. A tar member named e.g. `../../gitleaks` or `nested/dir/gitleaks` (a plausible malicious/repacked archive) would go undetected by the suite, which never asserts the binary lands at `destination/gitleaks` regardless of the member's internal path.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that packs a fake `gitleaks` executable under an archive member name like `nested/../gitleaks`, calls `_safe_extract_gitleaks`, and asserts the returned path is `destination/'gitleaks'`, the file exists, and its mode is 0o755.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the gitleaks download URL is https and the response status is 200 (non-empty) before verifying the digest.
evidence: scripts/install_review_scanners.py:237: `with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response, dest.open("wb") as fh:`
No scheme allowlist (https-only) or status check; the URL comes from the JSON manifest via `entry.gitleaks_url`.
Digest verification at line 315 does mitigate content substitution, so impact is bounded to the manifest being trusted input.
dropped.finding: `_download()` streams the response to disk with no HTTP status/size assertion before `_verify_digest` runs; while the digest check catches wrong content, `urllib.request.urlopen` on a redirect-to-error or a proxy interstitial that returns 200 with HTML would still be caught by the digest, but a truncated/empty download surfaces only as a generic digest mismatch. This is acceptable but the download performs no scheme restriction on the manifest `url` (an attacker-controlled manifest could point at file:// or http://).
scenarios: A tampered `review-scanners.lock.json` with a `file://` or `http://` gitleaks url is fetched by urlopen.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit timeout (e.g. `urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=...)`) to the Gitleaks downloader so a stalled release fetch fails fast instead of hanging builds/CI.
evidence: scripts/install_review_scanners.py:237: `with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response, dest.open("wb") as fh:`
No `timeout=` argument is passed; a stalled GitHub release fetch has no bound and hangs the `install` step run from Dockerfile.reviewbot:52 and `make scanner-integration`.
dropped.finding: The scanner downloader opens the Gitleaks release URL with urllib.request.urlopen and no timeout, so a slow or hung upstream download blocks the Docker image build and CI scanner lane indefinitely.
scenarios: GitHub release CDN is slow/unresponsive during an image build or the Verified scanner lane.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm `validate-locks` fails when the two requirements files disagree on the top-level `semgrep==` version.
evidence: docs/security.md: "Both requirement locks must keep the same top-level `semgrep==...` version, and the shared installer must invoke `pip install --require-hashes`."

ABSENCE: the diff wires `python scripts/install_review_scanners.py validate-locks` into CI but the truncated diff does not show validate-locks asserting cross-file semgrep-version equality; enforcement cannot be confirmed from the diff.
dropped.finding: The stated cross-lock invariant — both `review-scanners.<platform>.requirements.txt` files must pin the same top-level `semgrep==` version — has no diff-visible automated enforcement; it is documented only as a manual 'must'.
scenarios: A future Semgrep bump updates linux-amd64.requirements.txt but forgets linux-arm64.requirements.txt, leaving the Graviton review-bot on a divergent Semgrep version.

ABSENCE: the diff lists review-scanners.lock.json as changed but its JSON body is not present in the reviewable hunk (diff truncated).
dropped.finding: The Gitleaks lock provenance (per-platform version, asset arch, release URL, SHA-256, and checksums.txt source) claimed by docs cannot be verified from the diff because review-scanners.lock.json content was truncated.
scenarios: Reviewer approves the pin claim without confirming a real SHA-256 digest and a resolvable checksums.txt URL are actually present for both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 entries.

evidence: review-scanners.linux-amd64.requirements.txt: "requests==2.34.2"
review-scanners.linux-amd64.requirements.txt: "pydantic-core==2.46.5"
ABSENCE: the diff provides hashes but not a means to confirm these exact versions exist on PyPI with matching digests without external lookup.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the `ENV SEMGREP_SEND_METRICS=off` / `SEMGREP_ENABLE_VERSION_CHECK=0` lines above the scanner install/check RUN so the build-time `semgrep --version` runs with telemetry/version-check disabled.
evidence: infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:52-53: `RUN python /app/scripts/install_review_scanners.py install ... && python /app/scripts/install_review_scanners.py check --platform linux/arm64 --prefix /opt/review-scanners`
`check_scanners` calls `_run_version(... SEMGREP_BIN ...)` which runs `semgrep --version` (scripts/install_review_scanners.py:357, 284-287)
The disabling ENV lines are set only afterward: infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:56-57 `ENV SEMGREP_SEND_METRICS=off SEMGREP_ENABLE_VERSION_CHECK=0`
infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:52-53 hardcode `--platform linux/arm64` on both the install and check invocations
scripts/install_review_scanners.py:70-71 already supports Docker-native platform detection via TARGETOS/TARGETARCH: `if source.get("TARGETOS") and source.get("TARGETARCH"): return f"{...}/{...}"`
The provisioner supports both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (SUPPORTED_PLATFORMS, scripts/install_review_scanners.py:23), so the arch pin is a build-host assumption not enforced by the tooling.
dropped.finding: The Dockerfile runs the scanner `check` step (which executes `semgrep --version`) before the SEMGREP_ENABLE_VERSION_CHECK=0 / SEMGREP_SEND_METRICS=off environment variables are set, allowing a build-time telemetry/version-check phone-home that the adjacent comment claims is disabled.
merged_from: The review-bot Dockerfile hardcodes `--platform linux/arm64` for both install and check instead of deriving the platform from Docker BuildKit's TARGETARCH, so building the image on an amd64 host would install an arm64 gitleaks binary that cannot execute.
scenarios: Image build on a network-restricted builder where semgrep's version check hangs or errors, or where a build-time phone-home is undesirable.
dropped.suggested_fix: Reorder the Dockerfile so the two SEMGREP_* ENV lines precede the `RUN python ... install ... && ... check` step.
